fixes.row: Eternal life, said as had or given now
fixes.why: The Berean prints John 5:39 as “You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life.” The row states the verse as a present possession with no sign that it is the presumption Jesus goes on to answer. A reader would take the row’s claim as Jesus’s own.
fixes.fix: Move John 5:39 out of this row into “Every other use”, or keep it here with a note: “John 5:39 reports what the Jews presume (“you presume”); Jesus’s own words follow in 5:39b–40.”

fixes.row: Live by faith: “the righteous will live by faith”
fixes.why: Hab 2:4 is Hebrew אֱמוּנָה (faithfulness, per the report’s own note) and the New Testament verses quote it with Greek πίστις. The row equates the two words under one English heading, and the heading “Live by faith” is New Testament framing set on an Old Testament verse. The rabbi cannot hear Hab 2:4 on its own terms under this label.
fixes.fix: Relabel to “The righteous live by faithfulness (Hab 2:4, Hebrew אֱמוּנָה); the New Testament quotes it as “by faith” (Greek πίστις)”, and move Hab 2:4 to its own row or add that note to the row; keep Gal 2:20 with the New Testament verses.

fixes.row: The days of life, the years of life, a lifetime, a long life
fixes.why: These verses are listed in the row and also in “Other words” as Hebrew יוֹם (day, יָמִים in Ps 91:16). The hub says in the same page that the two are different words and must not be made one. Listed under a life heading they do exactly that.
fixes.fix: Remove these seven verses from the row so they appear only in “Other words translated life” (יוֹם); keep the row to the חַי verses it is built on, and check the row count (n) after.

fixes.why: The row’s doors are God, the Holy Spirit and the resurrection, but its verses name the Son and Christ (John 5:21 “the Son gives life”; Eph 2:5 and Col 2:13 “with Christ”). Under the by-hand rule for divine persons, the Son is missing from the doors while being named in the verses.
fixes.fix: Add the door “Jesus” (the Son, Christ) to this row, by hand, next to “God” and “the Holy Spirit”.

fixes.row: Christ and life: “I am the life”, “the resurrection and the life”, ...
fixes.why: The note lists the readings as “the Lord’s Supper, as faith in Christ, or as both”. Catholic and Eastern Orthodox readers take this verse of the Eucharist, and the Lord’s Supper is not their term for it. The list of readings is not even-handed until those traditions are named in their own words.
fixes.fix: Change the note to: “read as the Eucharist (the Lord’s Supper), as faith in Christ, or as both” and keep the rest, so each tradition’s own name for the reading stands.

fixes.row: A life for a life; a ransom (noun row 20)
fixes.why: The note says “The law asks a life for a life”. Jewish tradition (for example Rashi and the Mekhilta) reads ayin tachat ayin in Exod 21:22–25 as payment of compensation, not a literal life. The page states the Torah as asking a life while the rabbi’s reading of the same text is absent, which misleads on the text the rabbi reads.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: “Jewish readers from the rabbinic period take Exod 21:23–25 as compensation paid, not a life given; the page takes no side.”

fixes.row: Duplicated verses across the noun rows (rule 7)
fixes.why: The same verse sits under two headings: John 6:54 under “had now” and “now and later”; John 3:36, 1 John 5:11–12, John 6:35/6:48/6:51 under the “Christ and life” or “fountain” rows; 1 Tim 4:8 under “now and later” and “present life”; John 10:11–18, 15:13 and 1 John 3:16 under both “laid down” and “life for a life”. The same verse with two labels makes the rows say the same thing twice (rule 7).
fixes.fix: Keep each verse in the row whose label it best states and remove it from the other; for John 6:54 (named both ways in its own sentence) keep it in “now and later” only, with the row-12 note saying so.

fixes.row: Verb catch-all “Every other use” and noun rows
fixes.why: These verses are in a noun row (the living God; the fountain and living sacrifice) and again in the verb catch-all, so the same verse stands twice on one page. Rule 7 asks that rows which say the same thing be flagged, and a reader counting verses finds them inflated.
fixes.fix: Remove each of these from the verb “Every other use” list (the noun row holds them); recount n for that catch-all.

fixes.why: Rom 6:23 (“the gift of God is eternal life”) and John 3:16 (“have eternal life”) are the hub’s own words, but neither sits in the three side-by-side eternal-life rows; John 3:16 is in “Every other use” and Rom 6:23 under “Life set beside death”. The page sets three readings beside each other while leaving the two most-quoted sentences out of the comparison.
fixes.fix: Name both in the note on the “had now” row, with their tense as the Berean prints it (“gift … is eternal life”, “have eternal life”), and say the page takes no side on whether that “have” is now or later.

worker_points.point: Eternal life, now or to come or both: three rows side by side, each with a note
worker_points.why: The structure is right. John 5:39 is presented as a had-now fact though the Berean says “presume”, John 6:54 and 3:36 are duplicated across rows, and Rom 6:23 and John 3:16 are left out of the comparison.

worker_points.point: “Live by” the commandments beside “live by faith” (verb rows 3 and 4)
worker_points.why: The note on the commandments row is fair. The faith row equates Hebrew אֱמוּנָה with Greek πίστις under New Testament framing, which the rabbi and the rule on Old Testament framing both forbid; relabel and separate Hab 2:4.

worker_points.point: The book of life (Ps 69:28, Rev 3:5 beside Rev 13:8, 17:8)
worker_points.why: The note names both readings of blotting out and of “from the foundation of the world” and takes no side. Ps 69:28 has the heading in the Berean’s own words.

worker_points.point: The dead live again: Ezek 37, Rev 20:4–5, Job 14:14
worker_points.why: Ezek 37 is said to be interpreted by its own chapter, the note names readings for Rev 20 without choosing, and Job 14:14 is kept as a question.

worker_points.point: God makes alive: 1 Cor 15:22 “all”, Eph 2:5 and Col 2:13, John 5:21 “whom He wishes”
worker_points.why: The note is even-handed, but the doors omit the Son while the verses name him (by-hand rule); add the Jesus door.

worker_points.point: Christ and life: John 6:53 and the Lord’s Supper
worker_points.why: Name the reading as the Eucharist and the Lord’s Supper, so Catholic and Eastern Orthodox readers see their own term.

worker_points.point: A life for a life; a ransom: Matt 20:28, Mark 10:45, John 10:11–18, the census ransom
worker_points.why: The rabbi’s reading of Exod 21:23 (compensation, not a life) is not in the note; add it. The rest of the note is fine.

worker_points.point: The life is in the blood: Lev 17:11 and Gen 9:4–5 “lifeblood”
worker_points.why: The examples show the full Lev 17:11 with its atonement clause, and the note defers the reading to the blood and sacrifice cards.

worker_points.point: Rom 5:18 “life for all men” in the catch-all
worker_points.why: The note names the dispute on “all men” and takes no side.

worker_points.point: The breath of life; the Spirit of life (Gen 2:7 beside Rom 8:2, 8:6, John 6:63)
worker_points.why: The note says the page does not settle whether “spirit” is breath or the Spirit, which is the right caution.

worker_points.point: Prov 8:35 “whoever finds me finds life” in the path row
worker_points.why: The note says the verse is the voice of wisdom and that the wisdom card reads the chapter.
The text records the wish and does not answer it in the same verse; the row keeps them as written.

missing.what: The gift of God is eternal life (Rom 6:23) and “have eternal life” (John 3:16) are not in the eternal-life comparison; the note on the “had now” row should name both with their tense.

examples_checked: 28 of 30 labelled rows show their label in all four examples (read in the Berean text in the built hub); exceptions: “Weary of life” (1 Kgs 19:4 shows only “Take my life”) and “Livelihood” (Mark 12:44 and Luke 21:4 are the same sentence). The two catch-all rows have no label to check. Checked live with curl: John 5:39, Hab 2:4, Ps 91:16.
summary: The hub is faithful to the Berean and the contested points are set side by side with notes that take no side, so it is near ready. Eight fixes are needed before it ships: one presumption presented as fact (John 5:39), an Old Testament verse under a New Testament faith heading (Hab 2:4), yom verses inside a life row, verses that repeat across rows and across forms, and a few notes and doors that leave the Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and rabbinic readings unnamed.
